output.brief: The wrong expiry dates were not caused by operators or the printer firmware. A Regulatory Affairs edit on 3 Oct set Veltranol's shelf life to 36 months. It was meant to apply only to lots made from March 2027, but from 4 Oct the line integration service sent 36 months to the printers. The vendor said this could not happen, so the way it handles future-dated values needs checking. Printer logs show no operator overrides on any of the 17 affected jobs. They also show correct 24-month dates on the agency operators' earlier jobs. Two affected lots ran on Line 1 day shift with permanent staff, and those lots are in the warehouse. The camera only compares the print to the job data, so it passed every carton. Don't remove or warn the agency operators. Do reset the Veltranol shelf-life records and hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two on Line 1. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Inspect other products edited in October, especially the two with future-dated changes. Keep the camera check on. I'm fairly confident about the cause. Whether other products are affected is still unknown. A full 12-month reconciliation looks unnecessary for now, because the printer records show correct dates before 4 Oct.
